description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison between mBERT and XLM-R across various language families in terms of task count, categorized by whether mBERT performed better, XLM-R performed better, or both models performed the same. The horizontal axis lists language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents “task count,” ranging from 0 to 40 with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each language family has three bars: light blue for “mBERT better,” dark blue for “XLM-R better,” and light green for “same.” For example, in IE-Slavic, XLM-R significantly outperforms mBERT with a task count near 40, while mBERT is around 12 and “same” is around 28. In contrast, for IE-Baltic, XLM-R leads with ~10 tasks, mBERT has 0, and “same” is ~7. IE-Germanic shows mBERT at ~4, XLM-R at ~18, and “same” at ~22. IE-Romance has mBERT at ~4, XLM-R at ~13, and “same” at ~30. IE-Indic shows mBERT at ~1, XLM-R at ~5, and “same” at ~4. IE-other has mBERT at ~1, XLM-R at ~6, and “same” at ~8. Isolate shows mBERT at ~1, XLM-R at ~5, and “same” at ~1. Semitic has mBERT at 0, XLM-R at ~7, and “same” at ~1. Uralic shows mBERT at ~1, XLM-R at ~14, and “same” at ~5. The chart visually emphasizes that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across most language families, particularly in IE-Slavic and Uralic, while “same” performance is most frequent in IE-Romance and IE-Germanic.
